answer: One almond grove warden holds a grove for 120 days on a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license. Forty trees wear numbered steel bands, and an onyx marker stone at the gate proves each photo is on site. A falcon nest box above the gate is logged by rangers. The warden weighs the harvest, a neighbor signs the tally, and a ranger checks the book against the trees twice. A forged tally loses the deposit and bars the warden 180 days. Faking 10,000 groves freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A grove is a ledger planted in soil, and a fake warden finds its ground taken.
